title: SOS fingerprint is code + free-text habit name (or telemetry key), not a stable subject id — duplicate names silently suppress alerts, and renames can permanently evade escalation
description: sos_scan() builds each SOS fingerprint as f"{code}:{subject}" where subject is the habit NAME (habit_core.py:525-528, 542-546) for missed_daily/streak_broken, or the telemetry key for telemetry_stale (habit_core.py:559) — habit_core.py:566 `fp = f"{code}:{subject}"`. Habit names are free text with no uniqueness constraint (habits table has no UNIQUE on name, and add_habit accepts duplicates — verified by execution: two habits both named 'Water the plants' both overdue yields exactly ONE pending SOS, not two). The partial unique index `idx_sos_open_fp ON sos(fingerprint) WHERE status='pending'` (habit_core.py:79) then dedupes on that weak key, with the IntegrityError swallowed by a bare except (habit_core.py:575-576). Two real consequences on the designed trust path: (1) two distinct overdue habits sharing a name (e.g. an agent-influenced duplicate add, or a deliberate rename of one habit to another's name) collapse to a single alert — the second failing habit is invisible to the operator and to the cron responder until the first is acked (verified: after acking and rescanning, the still-broken second habit re-filed the first habit's fingerprint only; the second habit never alerted within the scan, and in a one-shot-scan pattern such as the cron monitor, the suppression window persists until the next scan+ack cycle). (2) A subject renaming itself between scans changes the fingerprint, letting the same recurring incident re-file as 'new' indefinitely — but the inverse is the alert-suppression direction an attacker-chosen name enables. The system's core safety property ('one pending row per failing condition, operator sees it after ack') silently breaks whenever names collide. Fix shape: fingerprint on code + habit_id (or readings key as a whitelisted identifier, not a free-form sensor name), and log the swallowed IntegrityError instead of a bare pass.

reasoning: SOS fingerprint now keys on the immutable subject id (habit:<id> / key:<name>) instead of the free-text habit name. Duplicate-named overdue habits file distinct SOS rows, and renaming cannot evade or suppress a pending row. Verified by test_sos_fingerprint_keyed_on_stable_id_not_name and test_sos_rename_cannot_evade_pending_row; 59/59 green.
